subject: polity
title: Constitutional Bodies of India
description: President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Parliament, Supreme Court, and other constitutional bodies

content.overview: Constitutional bodies are established by the Constitution of India. They have specific powers and functions defined in the Constitution.
keyPoints: President: Head of State, elected by Electoral College (MPs + MLAs), 5-year term
Vice President: Ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha, elected by MPs
Prime Minister: Head of Government, leader of majority party in Lok Sabha
Supreme Court: Highest judicial authority, established under Article 124
High Courts: Highest court in each state, established under Article 214
Attorney General: Highest legal officer, appointed under Article 76
Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG): Audits government accounts, Article 148
Union Public Service Commission (UPSC): Recruitment to civil services, Article 315
Finance Commission: Distribution of taxes between Union and States, Article 280

mnemonics.trick: P-V-P-S-C-A-E-U-F = President, VP, PM, Parliament, Supreme Court, CAG, AG, EC, UPSC, FC
mnemonics.explanation: Remember the order: President, Vice President, Prime Minister, Parliament, Supreme Court, CAG, Attorney General, Election Commission, UPSC, Finance Commission

quiz.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
quiz.explanation: Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha under Article 64

quiz.question: Which article establishes the Supreme Court of India?
quiz.explanation: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court of India

quiz.question: Who audits government accounts in India?
quiz.explanation: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audits all government accounts under Article 148

timeline.event: Constitutional bodies established with new Constitution
